# bitbucket_repository_runner (Resource)

Registers a self-hosted Pipelines runner for a single repository. This only registers the runner in Bitbucket and returns its OAuth credentials; installing and running the actual runner daemon/container is done outside of Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bitbucket_repository_runner" "api" {
  repository_slug = bitbucket_repository.api.slug
  name            = "payments-api-runner"
  labels          = ["self.hosted", "linux"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the runner.
- `repository_slug` (String) Slug of the repository this runner belongs to.

### Optional

- `labels` (List of String) Labels used to target this runner from bitbucket-pipelines.yml via runs-on.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier, formatted as "workspace/repository_slug/runner_uuid".
- `oauth_client_id` (String) OAuth client ID issued for the runner daemon to authenticate with.
- `oauth_client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth client secret issued for the runner daemon. Bitbucket only returns this once, at creation time; it is preserved in state afterwards and cannot be recovered if lost (re-create the resource to get a new one).
- `runner_uuid` (String) Bitbucket-assigned UUID of the runner.
- `status` (String) Current runner status as reported by Bitbucket (e.g. ONLINE, OFFLINE).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import bitbucket_repository_runner.api payments-api/{runner-uuid}
```
